issues.description: isIncluded mutates cache with state that depends on changedFiles — invariant violated when changedFiles changes mid-run
issues.detail: The globCache stores the final boolean `included`, which is now a conjunction of (matches glob) AND (filename in changedFiles). The cache key is only `filename`. The author handwaves this by clearing the cache in onTestRunStart, but the cache invariant — 'cacheHit reflects pure glob membership' — has been silently changed to 'cacheHit reflects glob membership conjoined with whatever changedFiles happened to be at insertion time'. State the precondition of the cache, or stop calling it a cache. If isIncluded is ever invoked before onTestRunStart fires (and the cache is non-empty from a prior run, watch mode, or a different code path), the result is wrong. There is no proof of the ordering.

issues.description: changedFiles membership test uses array .includes — O(n*m) where it should be O(n)
issues.detail: `this.changedFiles.includes(filename)` runs inside isIncluded, which is invoked once per candidate file. For a project of m source files and n changed files, this is O(n*m). A Set would make it O(m). This is not merely a performance nit; it is the symptom of writing code without stating the data structure required by the operation. The operation is set membership. Use a set.

issues.description: Smuggled goto: onTestRunStart is an optional side-effecting hook the caller must remember to invoke at three separate sites
issues.detail: Three call sites in core.ts now contain `await this.coverageProvider?.onTestRunStart?.()` immediately after `_testRun.start(...)`. The precondition of generateCoverage and of isIncluded now silently depends on this hook having been called. A fourth code path that starts a test run without the hook will produce incorrect coverage with no error. This is the classic smuggled goto: control flow that must occur but is enforced by convention rather than structure. Either fold it into _testRun.start, or have generateCoverage refuse to run if onTestRunStart has not been called with a precondition check.

issues.description: Postcondition of onTestRunStart is ambiguous when VitestGit.findChangedFiles returns null vs empty array
issues.detail: `this.changedFiles = changedFiles ?? undefined` collapses null into undefined, which means 'no filter applied — include everything'. But an empty array means 'no files changed — include nothing'. These are distinct postconditions and the code is silent about which it intends in the null case. If the user wrote `coverage.changed: 'HEAD'` and git returns null (e.g., not a git repo, error, no upstream), the resulting behavior is 'report coverage for everything' — exactly the opposite of what the user asked for. State the postcondition, or fail loudly when git cannot answer.

issues.description: Inheritance rule from test.changed to coverage.changed conflates 'not set' with 'set to false'
issues.detail: The resolver: `if (resolved.coverage.changed === undefined && resolved.changed !== undefined)`. The CLI transform returns the literal `false` for the strings 'false'/'no', which means a user explicitly passing `--coverage.changed=false` and also `--changed=HEAD` will get coverage.changed = false (correct). But the public.test.ts test only verifies the undefined→inherit case and the false→preserve case; it does not verify that a user-set true does not get clobbered, nor that mixing CLI and config file resolution preserves intent. The specification of the inheritance rule is not written down anywhere readable. Write it. Then prove it.

issues.description: CLI transform accepts 'true'/'yes'/'false'/'no' undocumented; rest of Vitest CLI does not
issues.detail: The transform silently accepts 'yes' and 'no' as boolean aliases. This is a folkloric convention not declared in the docs and not consistent with the rest of the CLI surface. Either document the accepted lexicon precisely, or restrict it to the two values the rest of the system uses. Inconsistency in a CLI is a small tax on every future reader.

issues.description: TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the added tests demonstrate the happy path but do not exercise the precondition violations
issues.detail: The new tests under test/coverage-test/test/changed.test.ts cover three positive scenarios. They do not cover: (a) coverage.changed set against a nonexistent git ref, (b) coverage.changed set in a non-git directory, (c) coverage.changed = true (boolean) which is documented as a supported value but never exercised, (d) interaction with watch mode where onTestRunStart fires repeatedly and changedFiles must be refreshed each time. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence; here the tests do not even attempt to show the presence of the bugs in the failure modes the documentation invites.

issues.description: cleanUrl change to isIncluded is unmotivated in the diff and silently widens the function's contract
issues.detail: The diff changes `slash(_filename)` to `slash(cleanUrl(_filename))` with no commit message rationale and no test added that specifically requires cleanUrl. cleanUrl strips query strings and hashes; this is presumably to handle the query-param transforms test, but the change is buried with no comment stating the precondition it now accepts (URLs with query params) or why the prior code was wrong. A reader cannot tell whether this is a bug fix orthogonal to the feature or a load-bearing part of it. State the reason in code or in commit.

review.summary: The feature is useful and the implementation is small, but it has been written rather than reasoned. Three classes of failure: (1) the cache invariant in isIncluded has been silently changed from 'pure glob result' to 'glob ∧ changed-set at insertion time' with no statement of the precondition, defended only by a cache.clear() call that the reader must trust will always run first; (2) onTestRunStart is a side-effecting hook the caller must remember to invoke at three separate sites — a smuggled goto enforced by convention; (3) the null/undefined/empty-array distinction in the git result is collapsed, meaning a git failure silently produces 'coverage everything', the opposite of the user's request. The tests demonstrate the happy path and ignore the failure modes the documentation explicitly invites. Refactor to make the precondition of generateCoverage explicit, use a Set for membership, and fail loudly when git cannot answer. None of this is shipping-blocking, but none of it is reasoned either. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.
